attack_games_n256.game: second preimage of the message hash Q = H(I||q||D_MESG||C||m) for a signed (C,m)
attack_games_n256.why: Grover on a fixed function, single target (C fixed by signer)

attack_games_n256.game: invert one LM-OTS chain node H(I||q||i||j||.) to lower a digit
attack_games_n256.why: single-target Grover; (I,q,i,j) prefix makes each node its own function

attack_games_n256.game: hash collision on Q to sign two messages with one OTS leaf
attack_games_n256.why: BHT with QRAM; but the attacker does not choose C, so a collision gives no forgery in EUF-CMA (recorded, not counted)

attack_games_n256.game: forge a Merkle path to a fresh leaf (second preimage on an interior node)
attack_games_n256.why: node prefix (I, r, D_INTR) fixes the function

attack_games_n256.game: find a message whose digit vector dominates a signed one (no inversion)
attack_games_n256.why: impossible: checksum strictly decreases when any digit increases

untestable_assumptions: A-NoExport: the private key state never leaves the hardware module (SP 800-208 §8.1); S1-009 shows the consequence if it does.
A-Grover: 2^(n/2) queries is optimal for unstructured search (BBBV 1997 lower bound — a theorem in the query model); the >= 2^18 gates/query floor is an engineering assumption.
A-SHA256: SHA-256 truncated to n bytes behaves as a random function for (second-)preimage; no structural attack better than generic is known.
